Provenance
Our Collegiate Arch motif is partly inspired by Take Ivy , the indispensable 1965 classic that defined a generation of style. Consisting of candid photos taken on Ivy League campuses, Take Ivy was an immediate sensation in its home country of Japan, invigorating nascent subcultures while serving as an indispensable historical record of midcentury American menswear. The book has been hailed by The New York Times as “a treasure of fashion insiders.” Our Collegiate Arch collection pays homage to the enduring influence of American campus style.

p-drakes-9524756218069.d:
A tweed blazer is one of those things you don’t know you need until you have one. It has that knack of being both rugged and refined, the kind of jacket you end up reaching for more than you ever expected.
Cut in Drake’s signature silhouette, it features a natural shoulder, subtle waist shaping, and a light construction that allows the jacket to move gracefully with the wearer.
Expertly tailored and fully canvassed with a hand-shaped chest, the jacket drapes naturally over the body, offering both shape and comfort. Hand-attached collars and sleeves provide a flexibility unmatched by machine construction, allowing the jacket to adapt seamlessly to the wearer, while a buggy lining ensures fluidity across the back and shoulders, and traditional lapels, with a wider profile and richer belly, reflect our time-honed house style.
Cut from 13.8oz Harris Tweed, woven by hand in the Outer Hebrides at one of the islands’ legendary mills, long regarded as the benchmark for authentic tweed.

First introduced in 1989, the New Balance 1500 marked a decisive moment in performance footwear design, marrying technical innovation with a streamlined, assertive profile. Produced in Flimby as part of the brand’s esteemed Made in UK line, the 1500v1 remains a quietly confident presence decades on.
In this ‘Vintage Sports’ edition, the silhouette takes on a richly tonal character. Deep green pigskin suede overlays sit atop breathable mesh, creating depth and texture and retaining the shoe’s original athletic intent while reflective detailing nods to its performance pedigree.
Underfoot, ENCAP midsole cushioning provides dependable support and structure, paired with a durable rubber outsole for everyday wear. The result is a heritage runner that feels as relevant now as it did upon its debut.

The chore jacket’s older sibling, the work coat traces its roots to early 20th-century workwear, shaped by the demands of the Industrial Revolution.
Cut from a rinse-washed 6.7oz cotton-linen cloth, the fabric has a soft, broken-in handle from the first wear, with a breathability and texture that comes into its own as the days grow warmer. The silhouette is deliberately boxy and relaxed, borrowing from the straightforward proportions of factory coats and workshop jackets, designed to layer easily and move without fuss.
Three patch pockets at the hip, plus an additional pocket at the rear, provide generous storage and nod to traditional atelier and studio garb, while raglan sleeves, corozo buttons, and a checked lining bring a quietly sartorial note.
The result is a working coat in spirit, but one that sits just as comfortably with tailoring as it does with denim.
